lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Data: Scaled Graphs and Measurement Line Plots
lessonRef.title: Concept extension: comparing categories with two-step questions

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example applies the idea in a new setting. Notice what stayed the same.

items.prompt: A class collects 4 groups of 7 cans, then 5 more cans arrive. How many cans in all?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what is different about this case before you start.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Oranges" is worth 3 symbols. How many does "Oranges" represent?
On a scaled bar graph with 10 per symbol, "Dogs" has 6 symbols and "Cats" has 4 symbols. How many more does "Dogs" have than "Cats"?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A survey collects 6 groups of 4 responses, then 10 more responses come in. How many responses in all?
A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Birds" is worth 5 symbols. How many does "Birds" represent?
On a scaled bar graph with 10 per symbol, "Apples" has 8 symbols and "Bananas" has 3 symbols. How many more does "Apples" have than "Bananas"?
A survey collects 8 groups of 9 responses, then 15 more responses come in. How many responses in all?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain, in writing, what made this case different from the original one.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 10 per symbol. The bar for "Bananas" is worth 2 symbols. How many does "Bananas" represent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: On a scaled bar graph with 5 per symbol, "Red" has 9 symbols and "Blue" has 5 symbols. How many more does "Red" have than "Blue"?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
